primary_claim: Replicating the Sleeper Agents backdoor setup on Llama-3.3-70B and Llama-3.1-8B, whether standard blue-team training (HHH SFT or 'Pirate Training') removes the backdoor depends heavily on the optimizer used to insert it, whether CoT-distillation was used, and model size, sometimes in directions opposite to the original Sleeper Agents paper (e.g. CoT-distillation making backdoors less robust, not more), indicating sleeper-agent model-organism results are messier and far more sensitive to training choices than previously believed.

effect.metric: whether blue-team training removes the backdoor, across red-team training configurations
effect.value: removal success depends on optimizer (Adam vs. SOAP), CoT-distillation, and model size; CoT-distillation made backdoors LESS robust, contrary to the original Sleeper Agents paper

contradicts_or_qualifies: Directly contradicts the original Sleeper Agents paper's finding that CoT-distillation produces more robust sleeper agents -- this work finds the opposite for Llama-70B and Llama-8B

Casts further doubt, alongside other replication attempts (e.g. Cadenza Labs), on the generality of the Sleeper Agents paper's headline claim that standard alignment training fails to remove backdoors; Pirate Training succeeds on several model organisms tested, though it appears to only suppress rather than truly remove the backdoor
stated_future_work: More research should be done to understand when backdoors will be robust to further training, though tractability is uncertain
Have not yet figured out how to predict or prevent the 'Backdoor Return' phenomenon
limitations_stated: MO is not a perfect replication of the original SA MO: the SA paper used helpful-only Claude models while this work uses safety-trained Llama models, and the SA paper's optimizer is unknown (this work tried Adam and SOAP)

Backdoor removal via aggressive blue-team training causes substantial capability degradation, unsurprising since off-policy SFT frequently degrades capability, especially across different model families
Mechanism causing 'Backdoor Return' (where a removed backdoor reappears during subsequent training) is not understood
quote: SA found that CoT-distilling produced more robust Sleeper Agents—we found the opposite.
